overview: Sigma 4.11's Bhop is a ten-mode horizontal speed module built on EventMove motion writes. The registered modes are Bhop, Hypixel, OnGround, OldHop, Mineplex, AAC, Janitor, Cubecraft, MineplexHop and AACWall, with MineplexHop gated behind a premium add-on that toggles the module off when absent; a 'Guardian' branch exists in onEnable but no such mode is registered, so it is unreachable. The hop family (Bhop, OldHop, Hypixel, AAC) re-jumps on ground ticks with a vanilla-shaped 0.42 motionY and pins horizontal speed to per-stage constants up to 1.35 plus the default speed, while OnGround and Janitor alternate 0.42 y offsets with 2.1 to 4.4 block-per-tick pins. The Mineplex mode is the outlier: it sends a C08 block placement at the feet every pre-update tick while grounded and moving, spoofs the held slot with C09, fills empty hotbar slots through windowClick, then pins motion at 0.35 or 0.44. An EventPacket handler watches incoming S08 teleports: it resets the stage counters, rewrites the teleport's yaw and pitch to the local values within a 300ms window, and when the LagBack setting is on, disables the module entirely.

sections.p: The module registers EventMove, EventUpdate, EventPacket and EventStep handlers plus an onEnable that seeds speed from MoveUtils.defaultSpeed and a stage of 2. EventUpdate pre measures lastDist as the horizontal delta between pos and prevPos each tick, which the hop modes use for their difference dampening. The EventPacket handler intercepts every incoming S08: it resets aacCount, count and jumps, sets stage to -4, and either toggles the module off (LagBack setting) or rewrites the teleport's yaw and pitch back to the local rotation inside a 300ms lastCheck window so the client's view does not snap. onDisable restores timerSpeed to 1 and applies per-mode decay (Mineplex re-syncs the held slot with C09, AACWall and cubecraft halve the horizontal motion). The dead Guardian branch in onEnable would have streamed a C04 down to y minus 10, but no Options entry names Guardian.

The Bhop mode jumps on stage 2 while grounded and moving with motionY 0.41999998688698 (plus the jump potion term) and multiplies the current speed by 1.533; stage 3 applies the difference damping 0.66 times lastDist minus the default speed, and later stages decay the speed by lastDist over 159. OldHop mirrors the shape with a 2.149 multiplier. Hypixel re-jumps at 0.407 plus the jump effect, computes getHypixelSpeed with a 0.64 jump-stage value, the 0.4145 firstvalue and a stage-over-500 decay, then scales by 0.91 and applies the less and lessSlow dampeners (0.11 per tick toward zero) and the collided reset. AAC re-jumps at 0.41999998688698 and escalates aacCount on each ground jump up to a cap of 4, with getAACSpeed adding 0.1069 and 0.046 at the jump stage and 0.06 to 0.04 window adders at higher jumps, plus an ice-block branch lifting the jump value to 0.59. Every mode floors its speed at MoveUtils.defaultSpeed.

Mineplex is a ground-only mode: while grounded, collided vertically, not jumping and premium, it runs invCheck and fills empty hotbar slots with bow ItemStacks via windowClick mode 2, calls MineplexSpoof to swap the held slot to the first free slot with C09 every 500ms, and sends an unconditional C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement at the feet position (y minus 1, face UP, hit vector 0.5/1/0.5) on every pre-update tick while moving, then pins motion to 0.44 with an empty hand or 0.35 with an item. In the air it zeroes motion and re-pins 0.35. OnGround sets timerSpeed to 1.085 and alternates an event y offset of 0.4198 or 0 on odd and even ticks with speed pins 2.1 and 1.3. Janitor alternates y plus 0.4 with pins 4.4 and 2.2. Cubecraft re-jumps on a 60ms step gate and decays speed as 0.35 minus stage over 200, and AACWall wall-hops with an onGround spoof and 0.37/0.575 pins.

files.label: Bhop.java
files.explanation: All ten registered modes, the stage machines and speed tables (getHypixelSpeed, getAACSpeed), the EventMove setMotion helper, the lastDist bookkeeping and the S08 lagback handler with the yaw and pitch rewrite and the LagBack self-disable. The Mineplex C08 feet placement, C09 slot spoof and windowClick bow fill, the dead Guardian branch and the premium MineplexHop gate are all in this file.

files.label: MoveUtils.java (shared speed engine)
files.explanation: MoveUtils provides defaultSpeed, getSpeedEffect, getJumpEffect, isOnGround and the setMotion overloads every mode calls, including the yaw decomposition that converts forward and strafe input into motionX and motionZ components. Because the helpers write the client motion fields, the effect reaches the server through the regular C03 position stream; the same utility backs the Sigma Highjump, Fly and Step modules, so the strafe math here is shared lineage.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (horizontal speed envelope)
countering.explanation:
There is no dedicated NCP Speed.java in this tree; the horizontal speed envelope lives inside SurvivalFly. check() derives the horizontal allowance from prepareSpeedEstimation, which predicts per-tick distance from the previous move with the 0.91 air inertia and the walk-speed acceleration raised by 0.3 for sprint, and handlePredictableMove compares the reported hDistance against hAllowedDistance. The violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) times 100, enforced with a set-back to the stored location.

Against the predicted sprint of about 0.28 to 0.31 blocks per tick, the Bhop mode's 1.35-plus-default jump pin produces an offset of roughly 1.0, the OnGround and Janitor pins of 2.1 to 4.4 are an order of magnitude over, and even the Mineplex 0.35/0.44 pins sit above the prediction, so the first move after a jump flags. The jump itself is credited (isJumpMotion arms a 10-tick jumpDelay), which is why the hop's vertical side passes; the horizontal pin is the tell. The S08 yaw and pitch rewrite is an honest counter-gap: it only preserves the client's look after a set-back teleport and does nothing about the envelope violation that caused the teleport.

countering.label: Speed (ground and air expectations)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Speed check builds a per-move expectation from getBaseMoveSpeed (0.2873, scaled by speed potions). On ground the expected distance is thisMove over groundTime (capped at 8) plus the base, and once groundTicks reaches 5 the onground_expected branch flags thisMove above the expectation; off ground the vertical speed selects a stage adder of 0.049, 0.08 below 0.34, or 0.3261 at and above 0.34. A sustained pin of 0.5 against the 0.3498 ground expectation flags within a few grounded ticks, and the Bhop mode's jump-tick values are far beyond that.

The air side is where the hop arc leaks: the descending stage allows only base plus 0.08, so the stage 3 and later hops with their damped but still elevated pins flag as the BunnyHop violation on the way down. The rising ticks get the 0.3261 grace, which is why the first ascent of each hop passes; the module's own decay curve (speed minus speed over 159) is far slower than the check's model and never converges back inside the window.

countering.label: Speed (momentum prediction discrepancy)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Speed check models momentum conservation: expected speed is friction times the last speed plus the force and adder terms, where friction is 0.91 in air and the block slipperiness on ground, and the adders include the vanilla 0.2 sprint-jump boost. The discrepancy between the reported speed and the expected value accumulates per player across moves, and once the total passes DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD (default 0.1) the check punishes and rubber-bands, with the violation level scaled by 10 times the discrepancy.

With a ground friction of 0.6 and an expected value around 0.33, a single grounded tick at the Bhop mode's pinned speed contributes a discrepancy of several tenths, crossing the 0.1 threshold on the first few updatePos moves; the hop modes that re-pin every tick accumulate instead of decaying. The jump and step exemptions only forgive the vanilla sprint-jump adder, never a magnitude pinned above it, and the no-move clamp (lastSpeed capped at 0.03 when the position is not updated) keeps stale high speeds from being carried into the next prediction.
